metadata.title: The Hahn-Banach Theorem: a proof of the equivalence between the analytic and geometric versions
metadata.authors: Fidel Jose Fernandez y Fernandez Arroyo

nodes.name: Seminorm
nodes.statement: A seminorm $p:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}$ on a real vector space $E$ is a function satisfying subadditivity and absolute homogeneity (norm-like, but possibly $p(x)=0$ for $x\neq 0$).
nodes.statement_clean: A seminorm is a norm-like nonnegative functional that may vanish off the origin.

nodes.name: Minkowski functional
nodes.statement: Given an absorbing set $D\subseteq E$, the Minkowski functional is $p(e)=\inf\{t>0\mid e\in tD\}$. When $D$ is open and absolutely balanced, $p$ is a continuous seminorm and $p(e)<1\Leftrightarrow e\in D$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Minkowski functional of a balanced convex open neighborhood of the origin is a continuous seminorm.

nodes.name: Hyperplane
nodes.statement: A hyperplane $H$ of a vector space $E$ is a vector subspace of codimension one, i.e., such that $E=H\oplus\langle z\rangle$ for some $z\in E\setminus H$.
nodes.statement_clean: A hyperplane is a codimension-one linear subspace.

nodes.name: Inductive ordered family $({A},\preceq)$
nodes.statement: On the family $A$ of pairs $(H,h)$ with $H$ a subspace of $E$ containing $L$ and $h:H\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ linear extending $f$ with $\vert h\vert\leq p$, define $(H_{1},h_{1})\preceq(H_{2},h_{2})$ iff $H_{1}\subseteq H_{2}$ and $h_{2}$ extends $h_{1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Order on extension pairs used to apply Zorn's Lemma in the analytic Hahn-Banach proof.

nodes.name: Family $B$ of subspaces avoiding $A$
nodes.statement: $B=\{L\subseteq E\mid L\text{ subspace},\ S\subseteq L,\ L\cap A=\emptyset\}$, ordered by inclusion.
nodes.statement_clean: Inductive family used in the Zorn-based proof of the geometric Hahn-Banach.

nodes.name: Cone $B=\bigcup_{\alpha>0}\alpha A$
nodes.statement: Given an open convex set $A\subseteq E$ with $A\neq\emptyset$, the set $B=\underset{\alpha>0}{\cup}\alpha A$ is open, convex, satisfies $\alpha B=B$ for every $\alpha>0$, and $B\cap S=\emptyset$.
nodes.statement_clean: Positive-cone hull of $A$ used to build the auxiliary seminorm.

nodes.name: Balanced neighborhood $D=(B-x)\cap(x-B)$
nodes.statement: For $x\in B$, the set $D=(B-x)\cap(x-B)$ is an open absolutely balanced (convex and balanced) neighborhood of the origin.
nodes.statement_clean: The intersection $(B-x)\cap(x-B)$ symmetrizes the cone into a balanced 0-neighborhood.

nodes.name: Hahn-Banach Theorem (analytic version, real case)
nodes.statement_latex: Let $E$ be a real vector space, $p:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}$ a seminorm, $L\subseteq E$ a subspace, and $f:L\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ linear with $\vert f(x)\vert\leq p(x)$ on $L$. Then there exists linear $g:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ extending $f$ with $\vert g(x)\vert\leq p(x)$ for every $x\in E$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every $p$-bounded linear functional on a subspace extends to a $p$-bounded linear functional on the whole space.
assumptions: $f:L\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ is linear with $\vert f(x)\vert\leq p(x)$ for every $x\in L$

nodes.name: Hahn-Banach Theorem (geometric version, real case)
nodes.statement_latex: Let $E$ be a real topological vector space, $A\subseteq E$ open and convex, and $S\subseteq E$ a subspace with $S\cap A=\emptyset$. Then there exists a hyperplane $H$ of $E$ with $S\subseteq H$ and $H\cap A=\emptyset$.
nodes.statement_clean: A subspace disjoint from an open convex set extends to a hyperplane disjoint from that set (Separation Theorem).
assumptions: $E$ is a topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$
$S\subseteq E$ is a subspace with $S\cap A=\emptyset$
conclusions: There exists a hyperplane $H$ of $E$ with $S\subseteq H$ and $H\cap A=\emptyset$

nodes.name: Equivalence of analytic and geometric Hahn-Banach (real case)
nodes.statement_latex: In the context of real topological vector spaces, the analytic and geometric versions of the Hahn-Banach Theorem are equivalent; in particular, the geometric version follows from the analytic version.
nodes.statement_clean: The two classical forms of Hahn-Banach are equivalent over real TVS.
assumptions: $E$ is a real topological vector space

nodes.name: Zorn's Lemma
nodes.statement_latex: Every nonempty inductively ordered set has a maximal element. Equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.
assumptions: $(X,\preceq)$ is nonempty and inductive (every chain has an upper bound)

nodes.name: Minkowski functional is a continuous seminorm
nodes.statement_latex: If $D$ is an open absolutely balanced neighborhood of the origin, then its Minkowski functional $p$ is a continuous seminorm and $p(e)<1\Leftrightarrow e\in D$.
assumptions: $D\subseteq E$ is an open, convex, balanced neighborhood of the origin

nodes.name: Decomposition properties of $M=G+\bigcup_{\alpha>0}\alpha A$
nodes.statement_latex: With $G$ maximal in $(B,\subseteq)$ and $M=G+\underset{\alpha>0}{\cup}\alpha A$: $A\subset M$, $M$ is open, $-M=G+\underset{\alpha<0}{\cup}\alpha A$, and $M\cap(-M)=\emptyset=M\cap G=(-M)\cap G$.
assumptions: $A$ is open, convex, nonempty, with $A\cap G=\emptyset$

nodes.name: $G$ is a hyperplane iff $E=G\cup M\cup(-M)$
nodes.statement_latex: Under the setup of the geometric Hahn-Banach proof, $G$ is a hyperplane of $E$ if and only if $E=G\cup M\cup(-M)$.

nodes.name: Proof of analytic Hahn-Banach via Zorn's Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Zorn's Lemma to the inductive family $({A},\preceq)$ of $p$-bounded linear extensions; show the maximal element $(G,g)$ has $G=E$ by contradiction, extending to $G\oplus\langle z\rangle$ if $G\neq E$.

nodes.name: Proof of geometric Hahn-Banach via Zorn's Lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Zorn's Lemma to $(B,\subseteq)$ to obtain a maximal subspace $G\supseteq S$ with $G\cap A=\emptyset$; use a connectedness argument on $f(t)=ta+(1-t)y$ to force $E=G\cup M\cup(-M)$, hence $G$ is a hyperplane.

nodes.name: Proof of analytic version from geometric version
nodes.statement: Reduce to $f\neq 0$ with $f(y)=1$. Apply the geometric Hahn-Banach to the open convex set $A=\{x\mid p(y-x)<1\}$ and to $\text{Ker}(f)$; the resulting hyperplane $H$ gives $E=H\oplus\langle y\rangle$ and the desired extension $g(x+ty)=t$.

nodes.name: Proof of geometric version from analytic version (main contribution)
nodes.statement: Construct the cone $B=\bigcup_{\alpha>0}\alpha A$, pick $x\in B$, form the balanced neighborhood $D=(B-x)\cap(x-B)$, take its Minkowski seminorm $p$, define $f$ on $L=S\oplus\langle x\rangle$ by $f(z+tx)=t$, verify $\vert f\vert\leq p$, apply analytic Hahn-Banach to extend $f$ to $g$, and show $H=\text{Ker}(g)$ is the desired hyperplane.

nodes.name: Reduce to $A\neq\emptyset$ and form the cone $B$
nodes.statement: If $A=\emptyset$ the claim is trivial; otherwise consider $B=\underset{\alpha>0}{\cup}\alpha A$, which is open, nonempty, convex, satisfies $\alpha B=B$ for every $\alpha>0$, and $B\cap S=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Choose $x\in B$ and form $D=(B-x)\cap(x-B)$
nodes.statement: For any $x\in B$, the set $D=(B-x)\cap(x-B)$ is an open absolutely balanced (convex and balanced) neighborhood of the origin in $E$.

nodes.name: Minkowski functional $p$ of $D$ is a continuous seminorm
nodes.statement: Let $p$ be the Minkowski functional of $D$. Then $p$ is a continuous seminorm and $p(e)<1\Leftrightarrow e\in D$.

nodes.name: Define $f:L\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ on $L=S\oplus\langle x\rangle$
nodes.statement: Set $L=\langle S\cup\{x\}\rangle$. Each $y\in L$ has a unique decomposition $y=z+tx$ with $z\in S$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Define $f(z+tx)=t$; then $f$ is well-defined, linear, and $f|_S\equiv 0$.

nodes.name: Apply analytic Hahn-Banach to extend $f$
nodes.statement: By the analytic Hahn-Banach Theorem applied to $(p,L,f)$, there exists a linear $g:E\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ extending $f$ with $\vert g(e)\vert\leq p(e)$ for every $e\in E$.

nodes.name: $H=\text{Ker}(g)$ is a hyperplane containing $S$
nodes.statement: Since $g(x)=f(x)=1$, $g\not\equiv 0$, so $H=\text{Ker}(g)$ is a hyperplane. For $z\in S$, $g(z)=f(z)=0$, hence $S\subseteq H$.

nodes.name: Minkowski value at $x$: $p(x)=1$
nodes.statement: In the proof of PP421.4, $x\notin D$ (since $0\notin B$) gives $p(x)\geq 1$; conversely $tx\in D$ for every $t\in(-1,1)$, so $x\in\overline{D}$ and $p(x)\leq 1$. Hence $p(x)=1$.

nodes.name: Equivalence $\vert g\vert\leq p\Leftrightarrow A\cap\text{Ker}(g)=\emptyset$
nodes.statement: For any linear $g$ extending $f$ (with $g(z+tx)=t$ on $L$), $\vert g\vert\leq p$ if and only if $A\cap\text{Ker}(g)=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Plane $\mathbb{R}^{2}$, open disc and origin
nodes.statement: $E=\mathbb{R}^{2}$, $A=\{(x,y)\mid(x-2)^{2}+y^{2}<2\}$, $S=\{(0,0)\}$. Then $B=\{(x,y)\mid x>0,\ \vert y\vert<x\}$, $\overline{x}=(1,0)$, $D=\{(x,y)\mid\vert x\vert<1,\ \vert y\vert<1-\vert x\vert\}$, Minkowski functional $p(x,y)=\vert x\vert+\vert y\vert$ (a norm). Hyperplanes $\text{Ker}(g)=\{x+by=0\}$ with $\vert b\vert\leq 1$ are exactly the lines through origin not meeting $A$.

nodes.name: $\mathbb{R}^{3}$, half-space and $z$-axis
nodes.statement: $E=\mathbb{R}^{3}$, $S=\{x=y=0\}$, $A=\{x>0\}$. Here $B=A$, $\overline{x}=(1,-3,0)$, $D=\{\vert x\vert<1\}$, Minkowski functional $\Psi(x,y,z)=\vert x\vert$ — a seminorm but NOT a norm. The unique separating hyperplane is $\{x=0\}$.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{C}[0,1]$ with pointwise convergence
nodes.statement: $E=\mathcal{C}[0,1]$ with pointwise topology, $S=\{f\mid f(0)=f(1)=0\}$, $A=\{f\mid f(1)<0\}$. With $h(x)=x-2\in A$, $D=\{f\mid\vert f(1)\vert<1\}$, Minkowski functional $\Psi(f)=\vert f(1)\vert$ — a seminorm but NOT a norm. The unique separating hyperplane is $\{f\mid f(1)=0\}$.
